Received wisdom must become patient speech and care for people in need

Verse 19 told the readers to be quick to hear. Verse 22 adds that hearing is not enough. One who only hears deceives himself. Verses 23–24 compare him to a man who sees his face in a mirror. He looks, goes away, and forgets what he was like. Verse 25 describes the doer, who looks into the law and continues. Verse 27 names what doing looks like: care for orphans and widows.
Favoring wealth and withholding help expose a faith that remains only words

Verse 14 asks whether a faith with no works can save. Verses 15–16 answer with a case. A brother or sister lacks clothing and daily food. Someone wishes them peace, warmth, and food, and gives nothing. The words are kind, and the body still has nothing. Verse 16 asks what good that is. Verse 17 applies the case: faith by itself, without works, is dead.
Small acts of speech require judgment that produces peace instead of rivalry

Verse 8 calls the tongue a restless evil. Verse 9 gives the evidence, and it comes from worship. With the tongue we bless our God and Father. With the same tongue we curse people. The verse says why the two cannot fit: people are made in God’s image. To curse the image while blessing the one it reflects is a contradiction. Verses 11–12 add that a spring does not give two kinds of water.
Conflicting desires and confident plans must answer the limits of human control

Verse 13 quotes merchants who plan a city, a year, trade, and gain. Verse 14 gives two facts against the plan. They do not know tomorrow, and their life is a vapor. Verse 15 does not forbid planning. It gives the sentence they should say first: “If the Lord wills.” Even living is put under that condition, before “do this or that.” Verse 16 names the fault in the first speech: it was boasting.
Unpaid wages and shared prayer place endurance within care for wronged and vulnerable people

Verses 1–3 warn the rich that their stored wealth will witness against them. Verse 4 names one source of that wealth. Laborers mowed their fields, and the pay was kept back by fraud. Two things cry out: the wages and the reapers. The cries reach “the Lord of Armies,” a title of power. Verse 6 adds that the righteous one does not resist them. Verse 7 then tells the brothers to be patient until the Lord comes.
